  1                                  DIRECT TESTIMONY OF

 2                                  J. CURTIS HENDERSON

 3                        I.   BACKGROUND AND INTRODUCTION

 4     Q.   PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND IF YOU ARE CAPABLE OF GIVING

 5          TESTIMONY IN THIS MATTER.

 6     A.   My name is J. Curtis Henderson. I am over 18 years of age, am of sound mind, and am

 7          capable of providing this direct testimony. The facts stated herein are within my personal

 8          knowledge and are true and correct.

 9     Q.   ON WHOSE BEHALF ARE YOU PROVIDING THIS TESTIMONY?

10     A.   I’m testifying on behalf of myself and my wife Kimberly Henderson, and our San Saba

11          River Ranch, owned by Henderco L.L.C., Intervenors.

12     Q.   WHY ARE YOU PARTICIPATING IN THIS PROCEEDING?

13     A.   I am participating because the proposed 765-kV electrical transmission line routes that

14          include Link L4 would cross our property and would directly and negatively affect our home,

15          our livestock, wildlife, not to mention the devastating effects of runoff and associated

16          flooding on the San Saba River. Links M22 is part of the Applicants proposed route that

17          come very close to our property lines. The Commission needs to understand there are better

18          alternatives to supply electricity to the Permian Basin without ruining hundreds of miles of

19          the Texas Hill country and the pristine San Saba River .

20     Q.   PLEASE       DESCRIBE       YOUR       BACKGROUND           AND     CONNECTION          TO

21          MCCULLOCH COUNTY.

22     A.   My wife and I purchased our property in 2016 and have spent the time since then investing

23          in, improving, building on and enjoying our San Saba River Ranch with the intention of



     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                         2                    DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349                                          HENDERCO LLC
  1          passing on the heritage, legacy and love of our family ranch to the next generations.

 2     Q.   WHY DO YOU FEEL IT IS IMPORTANT TO OFFER THIS TESTIMONY?

 3     A.   The decisions made in this proceeding will have a direct, long-term impact on how we and

 4          our neighbors in McCulloch County live and operate on our lands. I want to make sure the

 5          Commission understands what is actually on the ground and how these 765-kV electrical

 6          transmission lines routes would affect us day to day.

 7                              II. PROPERTY AND LAND USE

 8     Q.   PLEASE DESCRIBE YOUR PROPERTY IN THE AREA.

 9     A.   This part of the Hill Country has rough terrain, native pasture, and established

10          improvements that support our ranching operation. Our San Saba River Ranch is divided

11          into multiple pastures and tracts with fencing, water sources, and internal roads that we rely

12          on to manage livestock and wildlife and move around the ranch. The single greatest natural

13          feature is the San Saba River. Our Home and cabins sit directly on and overlook the river.

14          It is simply pristine and beautiful.

15     Q.   HOW DO YOU AND YOUR FAMILY CURRENTLY USE THE PROPERTY?

16     A.   Cattle is run along the river and the and the interior pastures including under the proposed

17          L4 segment. There is the long-term unknown effect on cattle that graze under these

18          proposed 765-kV electrical transmission lines which in turn could adversely affect the cattle

19          industry and beef production. In addition to ranching, the property supports native wildlife,

20          including whitetail deer, dove, quail, axis deer, and wild turkey, which are part of the overall

21          use and appeal of the land to us.

22                III.   OVERVIEW OF THE PROJECT AND ROUTE 894

23     Q.   ARE YOU FAMILIAR WITH THE ONCOR/LCRA 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE

24          PROJECT PROPOSED BY THE APPLICANTS?

     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                           3                    DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349                                            HENDERCO LLC
  1     A.   Yes.

 2     Q.   ARE YOU AWARE THAT THE APPLICANTS HAVE IDENTIFIED ROUTE 894

 3          AS THEIR PREFERRED ROUTE?

 4     A.   Yes. I understand that the Applicants have identified Route 894 as the route that best meets

 5          the Commission’s routing criteria.

 6     Q.   DO YOU OPPOSE ROUTE 894?

 7     A.   Yes, we oppose L4 and M22 and all proposed routes and the project in total. It is

 8          unnecessary, a waste of money and destructive to our health and environment. The

 9          estimated $90 billion dollars it would cost to construct these lines to the Permian Basin

10          would be better spent better spent actually building natural gas powered electric plants in

11          the Permian Basin where natural gas is plentiful and cheap. L4, M22 and route 894 are not

12          in the best interest of the State of Texas. Water becomes more precious to Texas residents

13          every year. The San Saba River and the Hickory Aquifer are prime examples of possibly

14          endangered pristine water features. To jeopardize any water for future use by future

15          generations is unconscionable and immoral.

16          Secondly, this route selection financially harms all tax paying residents and all landowners

17          in McCulloch County. It is undeniable that these monstrous transmission structures and

18          lines will devalue the most pristine, highest priced land in the county. As a result, tax

19          revenue will decrease, causing new higher rates for all taxpayers in the entire county. The

20          impact will not stop there. I doubt that our hunting licensees will want to continue at current

21          rates with such transmission line rights of way robbing them of prime hunting areas. You

22          can also add to this lost revenue for all merchants (grocery, hardware, restaurants, retail,

23          etc.), due to the decrease in numbers of vacationers and hunters who once used facilities in

24          the San Saba River corridor.

     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                          4                    DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349                                           HENDERCO LLC
  1          IV.   ROUTES OPPOSED BY SUZANNE C. AND BRUCE L. JAMES

 2     Q.   ARE THERE ROUTING COMPONENTS THAT YOU OPPOSE?

 3     A.   Yes, we strongly oppose L4, M22 and generally the entire project but certain routes in

 4          particular that would harm the San Saba River.

 5     Q.   WHAT ROUTES DO YOU OPPOSE?

 6     A.   How would the transmission line affect our ranch:

 7          Our San Saba River Ranch is situated Section 122, P. Honig A-489; Section 123, J. Othold

 8          A-1093 and Section 49, G.H. & S.A.R.R. Co., A-427 in McCulloch County, Texas. We are

 9          members of Friends of The San Saba River (FOSS) with the goal of protecting the flow of

10          water in the San Saba River. Initially and still in the fight today, we have urged our Texas

11          government officials to help stop illegal pumping and excessive permit taking, creating

12          highly reduced river water flow issues affecting horse and cattle water availability, reducing

13          wildlife movement along the river while increasing hog traffic, and threatening the

14          endangered mussels in the river.       Now our emphasis is shared in stopping 765kV

15          transmission lines in the river corridor and crossing the river. Very little attention has been

16          given by Oncor/LCRA to extreme flood damage, erosion, and endangered species

17          destruction in a proven flood prone zone. No explanation of these truly potential concerns

18          has been given by the utilities.

19          The 765 kV line L4 would literally split our ranch in half, and we would be forced to pass

20          under it as we ingress and egress from our home. It would increase the likelihood of flooding

21          by removing acres of land filled with trees and vegetation that would be removed and no

22          longer be there to prevent runoff. At the L4 location, the land continues a drop off to the

23          San Saba River. The 765 kV line M22 would be north of our property across the river,

24          directly in our view.

     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                          5                    DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349                                           HENDERCO LLC
  1             All views would be destroyed, and our beautiful view is a great part of what we enjoy. Also,

 2             the transmission line would cross the Hickory Aquifer and water troughs that water the

 3             livestock and wildlife on the ranch. Any loss of water (quantity or quality) in our Hickory

 4             Aquifer would greatly destroy the value of this ranch.

 5             Route 894 is still in the San Saba River corridor. Any movement south would be a disaster

 6             to this ranch and the pristine San Saba River. Several years ago, AEP Texas (AEP)

 7             constructed a 138 kV transmission line in McCulloch and Menard Counties. It is a very ugly

 8             steel monopole type with four separate lines that split our ranch in half. This part of the

 9             proposed L4. For many years we hunted in that pasture, where we had a blind and the feeder

10             near the old, smaller AEP transmission lines. We harvested many trophies buck white tail

11             deer from that blind prior to construction the AEP 138 kV transmission line. Subsequently,

12             the deer activity decreased at that feeder. I believe it is because of those transmission lines

13             and the same thing or worse will happen with Oncor/LCRA’s proposed monstrous 765kV

14             lines. That feeder and blind were destroyed in the July 4, 2025 flood.

15     Q.      WHY ARE THE ROUTES YOU IDENTIFIED A CONCERN TO YOU?

16          A. ROUTE ANALYSIS

17          Despite the large number of filed routes, many which were not disclosed prior to their

18          Application, the Application by Oncor/LCRA confines a 214 to 244-mile, unprecedented first

19          time 765-kV project to a narrow study area that funnels alternatives into a few convergent

20          corridors, and fails to consult Texas Parks and Wildlife Department resources as they should

21          have done.

22          L4, M22, route 894 as well as all other possible routes suggested by Oncor/LCRA is a poor

23          selection primarily because it runs along the pristine San Saba River corridor with its beauty

24          and many benefits and crosses the highest land values property in McCulloch County, Texas.

     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                             6                    DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349                                              HENDERCO LLC
  1          Oncor and LCRA’s have literally zero experience with a 765kV line. Surely it would be more

 2          cost effective to build natural gas electrical power plants in the Permian Basin where there is a

 3          plentiful amount of cheap natural gas. Chevron Corporation and Microsoft Corporation recently

 4          agreed to a proposed natural gas-fired power plant designed to meet the growing energy needs

 5          of AI-driven infrastructure in the Permian Basin.

 6          Final Route: If there has to be such a transmission line going from east to west as

 7          proposed: Why not go north of Brady along the proposed Interstate-14 corridor. There is no

 8          waterway remotely comparable to the San Saba River north of Brady. The land is relatively flat

 9          land, less rock, and good soil for digging. There are existing easements (i.e. Interstate 14) that

10          could be used. Land acquisitions and valuations would be less.

11     Q.      ARE THERE ROUTES UNDER CONSIDERATION THAT AVOID YOUR

12             PROPERTY ENTIRELY?

13     A.      Yes. As I understand it, there are routes, including the Applicants’ preferred route, that do

14             not cross my property. That tells me it is possible to route this line without impacting our

15             ranch and the San Saba River

16                       V.    IMPACTS OF ROUTES UTILIZING LINK L4

17     Q.      WHY DO YOU NOT SUPPORT ROUTES UTILIZING LINK L4?

18     A.      I do not support those routes because they would impose the 765-kV transmission line

19             directly onto and across our ranch and are too close to the San Saba River. The way those

20             links are laid out, they cut through the middle of our property, through areas that we actively

21             use every day, and much too close to our home. That would interfere with how we live, how

22             we enjoy the land, and how we operate the ranch.

23     Q.      HOW WOULD THESE LINKS AFFECT YOUR HOME AND IMPROVEMENTS?

24     A.      Link L4 would be constructed very near to our home and related improvements. This

     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                              7                   DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349                                              HENDERCO LLC
  1          portion of the line crosses the San Saba River and would very likely contribute to future

 2          flooding during significant rainfall as occurred in July of 2025. The line will be highly

 3          visible from most areas on our ranch. It would be within the area we use the most for cattle

 4          raising, deer and turkey hunting, and see every day in our travels around the ranch moving

 5          cattle, checking water lines, etc. It would permanently change the character of our property,

 6          affect the enjoyment of our property, affect the value of our property and put a huge burden

 7          on our ranch and how we live. Link M22 would be constructed directly north of our home

 8          across the river. This portion of the line would very likely contribute to future flooding

 9          during significant rainfall as occurred in July of 2025. The line will also be highly visible

10          from most areas on our ranch.

11     Q.   HOW WOULD THESE LINKS AFFECT YOUR RANCHING OPERATION?

12     A.   This proposed route will disrupt how we move livestock, manage grazing, and maintain the

13          ranch as well as wreak havoc during hunting seasons. It creates obstacles that we have to

14          work around every day.

15     Q.   HOW WOULD THE TRANSMISSION LINE AFFECT YOUR ABILITY TO

16          MANAGE LIVESTOCK AND FENCING?

17     A.   We have miles of fencing that we rely on to manage cattle and hunting. Bringing a

18          transmission line through the property would certainly add new crossings, some new gates,

19          and areas that have to be maintained differently. Even if gates are grounded or built a certain

20          way, construction of this power line across our ranch will complicate things greatly. It is

21          more work, more maintenance, and more risk when handling livestock and hunters around

22          that kind of infrastructure.

23     Q.   HOW WOULD THESE LINKS AFFECT THE OVERALL USE AND VALUE OF

24          YOUR PROPERTY?

     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                          8                    DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349                                           HENDERCO LLC
  1     A.   Our San Saba River Ranch is something we intend to keep in the family for generations.

 2          Running a large 765-kV transmission line through the middle of our ranch affects how the

 3          property can be used and how it is viewed and how it will be transferred to our descendants.

 4          It fragments the ranch, creates a permanent visual impact, and changes the character of the

 5          land. That is not something you can undo. It will definitely have devastating effect on the

 6          overall monetary value of the property.

 7     Q.   HOW WOULD THESE LINKS AFFECT THE VISUAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL

 8          CHARACTER OF YOUR PROPERTY?

 9     A.   This is open ranch country, and part of its value is the natural setting. A 765-kV line is not

10          something that blends into the landscape. It is a large, highly visible structure that would be

11          seen across the ranch. That kind of visual impact affects not only us, but also the wildlife

12          and the overall character of the area. It will definitely have devastating effect on the overall

13          monetary value of the property.

14     Q.   HOW WOULD THESE LINKS AFFECT WILDLIFE AND OTHER USES OF

15          YOUR PROPERTY?

16     A.   The property supports native wildlife including whitetail deer, dove, quail, axis deer, and

17          wild turkey. Those are part of how the land is used and maintained. A large transmission

18          line running through the ranch changes movement patterns and disturbs those uses. It will

19          have a negative effect on the wildlife.

20     Q.   ARE THERE ADDITIONAL RISKS OR CONCERNS ASSOCIATED WITH

21          THESE LINKS?

22     A.   Yes. I have safety concerns about bringing a 765-kV high-voltage line onto our ranch where

23          people, equipment, livestock and wildlife are moving around daily. We would have to

24          operate around that infrastructure at all times. It adds a level of risk and concern that is not

     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                             9                  DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349                                            HENDERCO LLC
  1           there today. No specific health information is available about these new 765 kV lines.

 2           We’ve seen testimony about smaller lines passing electricity to ranch fences. What will

 3           these huge lines do? What happens to the river water and its inhabitants? What about a

 4           metal vehicle touching the river under these huge lines? What about a near deer blind?

 5           What about ground water or water troughs close to these lines? What about people with

 6           certain health issues known or unknown having to spend time in close proximity to these

 7           lines? We hear no information exists acknowledging a problem. But, does information

 8           exist that it is not a problem? Neither the utilities nor the PUC has shared any of this

 9           information in the voluminous papers of “word salad” to date.

10     VI.   JULY 4, 2025 FLOOD

11     Q.    DO YOU RECALL THE SAN SABA RIVER FLOOD OF JULY 2025.

12     A.    Yes, I do.

13     Q.    WHAT IS YOUR HISTORY WITH THE SAN SABA RIVER?

14     A.    We purchased the River Ranch in 2016, primarily due to the beauty of the San Saba River.

15           It was a lifelong dream come true. The pristine beauty of the river and wildlife along and in

16           the river was and still is something to behold.

17     Q.    PLEASE DESCRIBE THE FLOOD OF JULY 4, 2025.

18     A.    The San Saba River rose high enough to wash items off the porch of our main house. It

19           also flooded one of the cabins. During the 2018 flood, which was considered a 500 year

20           flood, the water was at least 10 feet below the 2025 flood. In some places up to 400 yards on

21           our side of the river the devastation was catastrophic. Hundreds of trees along the river were

22           removed, others were bent and in disarray, and others had debris on the top of their limbs. Upstream

23           Furniture and boats were found in our pasture, while our furniture, deer feeders and blinds washed

24           away downstream. New piles upon piles of rock appeared in the river in huge gatherings, some of


     PUC DOCKET NO. 59475                             10                    DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
     SOAH DOCKET 473-26-16349                                               HENDERCO LLC
  1          which changed the original stream of the river.

 2     Q.   HOW LONG DID IT TAKE TO CLEAN THE DEBRIS FROM THE FLOOD OF JULY 4,

 3          2025?

 4     A.   Beyond the personal clean up, the state and FEMA announced their intent to clean the

 5          debris. A month later FEMA stated and after three weeks the debris was removed, not

 6          burned.

 7     Q.   DID THE CLEAN-UP CREWS GET ALL OF THE DEBRIS REMOVED FROM YOUR

 8          L BAR FAMILY RANCH ALONG THE SAN SABA RIVER?

 9     A.   FEMA did a good job, but No. They were just not able to leave the land as a good steward

10          landowner would wish. There was no way for FEMA to stop the invasion of the new evasive

11          weeds and grasses that began from newly delivered seeds.

12     B.   Q.      ANY OTHER CONCERNS?

13     A.   Halff Associates published a publication, Assessing the Flood Events of Central TX July 4-

14                                      VII. CONCLUSION

15     Q.   WHAT IS YOUR REQUEST TO THE COMMISSION?

16     A.   We respectfully ask the Commission to avoid approving any requested route suggested by

17          Oncor/LCRA and particular any that includes or that uses Link L4 and Link M22. Those

18          routes would bring this 765-kV transmission line onto and across our property and directly

19          impact on our home and our ranching operation. There are other routes available, including

20          the Applicants’ preferred route, which avoids our property entirely. Based on that, this line

21          can feasibly be routed in a way that does not impact our ranch, and we ask that it be done

22          that way.

23     Q.   DOES THAT CONCLUDE YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY?

24     A.   Yes.
